extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, disciplinary counsel, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO final order imposing reciprocal discipline on a registered patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state-court censure; describes the notice/response procedure, grounds relied upon, and publication/notification obligations. Useful for understanding when and how the USPTO imposes identical discipline based on out-of-office disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The violation consisted of having been publicly censured by the Supreme Court of Arizona for misconduct (as described in the Arizona Disciplinary Commission Report and Hearing Officer's Report). The specific misconduct included advising a client to discontinue making payments to an ex-spouse in violation of a court order. This finding is the basis for the USPTO imposing reciprocal discipline (a public reprimand) pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline process under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order informed Respondent that the OED Director filed a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 requesting imposition of reciprocal discipline (public reprimand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice directed that if Respondent seeks to contest imposition of identical discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), Respondent must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If no genuine issue of material fact is shown, the Director may impose identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to show a 'genuine issue of material fact' to avoid identical discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: To contest imposition of identical discipline, the Respondent must establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must be filed within 40 days and contain all information the Respondent believes sufficient to establish such a genuine issue. Failure to timely file such a response can lead to a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that identical discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct categories cited by the state court as disciplinary grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arizona Supreme Court (via the Disciplinary Commission and Hearing Officer) concluded Respondent violated: (1) Ethics Rule 8.4(a) (violating a rule of professional conduct), (2) Ethics Rule 8.4(d) (engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice), and (3) Rule 53(c) (knowingly violating any rule or order of the court).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The underlying factual example given: advising a client to discontinue making payments to an ex-spouse in violation of a court order. These are the types of conduct that, when resulting in public censure elsewhere, can trigger reciprocal discipline under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and 35 U.S.C. § 32
rubrics_metrics.description: When reciprocal discipline is imposed, the OED Director shall publish the Final Order and provide notice of the public discipline and reasons for it to relevant authorities and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the OED Director shall: publish the Final Order; publish a notice in the Official Gazette (a Notice of Reprimand describing the practitioner, registration number, the basis for the reprimand, and statutory/regulatory authority); post disciplinary decisions in the OED Reading Room; and give notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond to the Notice within the prescribed time
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent failed to file a response to the Notice and Order within 40 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Respondent did not file a response, the Director determined that there was no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and concluded that a public reprimand was appropriate. Thus, non-response can be treated as a basis for entering reciprocal discipline without further factual dispute.
